I don't get the ratings, but for regular/sane people, this is a great, FREE extension. I've used it on multiple browsers and devices for 2-3 years. Tab/Session extensions have gotten ridiculously complicated. Tab Session Manager checks every box I wanted this time around: auto-save sessions (and limits), cloud backups, exports, setting startup behavior and what is saved/loaded, and no need to create an account. Most importantly, it's simple. Users generally don't want a persistent tab/sidebar for journaling and organizing every random tab they leave open.

Personally, I just want my window(s) back after Chrome updates or crashes, and this does it well. I periodically export my sessions and settings because stuff happens, but I think I've had one problem in 3 years, and it was Google's fault, so it was a quick restore from the sync (or caution backup, can't remember). Tabmanager.io is a good app that does a lot, but I (like many others) don't want to pay, and it was kind of overkill.

Many of the bad reviews are by people expecting their browser to be its own perfect OS, and don't understand that users bear responsibility for poor browser hygiene. Close your damn tabs if it's something innocuous. If session restoration causes performance problems, you shouldn't use Chrome. The tab group concerns for those who are into that are valid.
